newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Undervalued stocks lead Russian bull market.
newsitem.headline: Undervalued stocks lead Russian bull market.

text.p: Experienced Russian investors are moving into undervalued regional stocks and new funds are flowing into leading issues, keeping the stock market on course for new records, traders and analysts say.

Hedge funds, brokers and other investors who have been in the Russian market for a year or more are moving money into secondary shares, making quick windfalls as the market follows their attention and revalues them.
"Every day you see a regional telecom or energo (utility) shoot up like a star," said one senior trader, who believes that obscure stocks would continue to lead the market.
The Russian Trading System's RTS-2 stock index has risen more than 50 percent this year, and on Friday continued to closed in on its record high of 312.66.
But on most days this year the biggest winners have been among 90 telecommunications and 90 utilities, which can rise by 20 percent or so in a single day.
The illiquid shares have been bouncing up, independent of a company's growth potential.
"So it goes -- every day someone comes with new money and that has a big effect on the secondary shares. People do not care about fundamentals," the trader said.
